claims.text: The rider's own chat message asked the driver to stop at Jurong Point first, and the driver agreed. Under POL-RD-04 the deviation is exonerated to the extent it is attributable to that rider instruction, so the excess distance between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor must be excluded before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied.

The rider instruction satisfies POL-RD-04(a) to (c): it came from the rider (MSG-02811-001, sender RIDER), it was sent at 06:33:18, only 60 seconds after the meter started at 06:32:18 and well before the vehicle left the optimal corridor, and it names a specific place, 'Jurong Point', carried as a resolved waypoint_hint at lat 1.305461, lng 103.90726.

The gps_trace corroborates the instruction as POL-RD-04 requires: the vehicle passes within 21.70 m of the requested waypoint at fix index 104, timestamped 2026-08-17T06:49:38, far inside the 200 m threshold set by POL-RD-04. The corroboration test is therefore satisfied and the clause is available.

The rider's claim that this was 'a tour' rather than a quick stop is contradicted by the record: the only waypoint the trace approaches is the one the rider herself named, and the driver's counterparty statement that 'the rider asked for the stop, it is in the chat' is borne out by the chat log. The rider cannot recover for a detour she requested.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and has shown the artifacts describe the same trip with matching trip identifier TRP-02811 across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, and an excess of 6.09 km / 30.0% over the 20.3 km optimal. That shifts the burden to the driver, and the driver has discharged it by pointing to the chat_log and POL-RD-04.

The trace is clean for policy purposes: 207 fixes at a 10 second sample interval, 100.0% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, so POL-RD-07(a) to (c) are not met and the deviation is measured on the trace as recorded rather than on any impaired stretch.

No traffic advisory covers this trip window: the only advisory artifact in the bundle is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and no payload, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and no external traffic cause can reduce the excess. The driver does not rely on one, and the rider's recovery, if any, must come from the rider-requested detour analysis under POL-RD-04.

The fare is METERED, not upfront-quoted, so POL-RD-11 does not close the distance-refund route and POL-RD-02 is the operative arithmetic clause. The recomputed fare on the booked optimal route is 27.4970 against a charged_total of 34.00, a refund of 6.5030, which rounds up to 6.55 payable and is above the 0.50 de minimis.

The refund under POL-RD-02 is 6.5030, which is 19.13% of charged_total and well below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is a PARTIAL_REFUND and not a FULL_REFUND. The rider is not entitled to the whole 34.00.

No ERP or toll line is in dispute: the fare_breakdown carries zero ERP gantries and a zero tolls_erp figure, so POL-RD-09 pass-through corrections add nothing to the rider's recovery and there is no billing-integrity defect to refer.

The driver's profile does not establish a repeat deviation pattern under POL-RD-06: deviation_flags_90d is 1, below the threshold of 3, and 1 divided by completed_trips_90d of 348 is 0.0029, below the 0.05 ratio. No FULL_REFUND uplift and no conduct referral is licensed on this record.

The rider's profile does not trigger the POL-RD-08 corroboration requirement: deviation_claims_60d is 1, below the threshold of 4, so the claim is not one that requires corroboration beyond the gps_trace. The rider's claim is nonetheless defeated on the merits by the rider-requested detour, not by her filing history.

The rider's claim that she 'only asked for a quick stop, not a tour' is not supported by the record on the distance she contests: the excess of 6.09 km is the distance to and from the waypoint she named, and POL-RD-04 excludes exactly that stretch. To the extent the rider seeks the full 9.00 contested, the record does not support it and that part of the claim should be rejected.

ruling.explanation:
Decision for trip TRP-02811. Both parties are told the same thing: the record shows the rider asked for the stop, so the fare she contests stands.

What was measured. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-02811) ran 26.39 km against a 20.3 km platform optimal, an excess of 6.09 km, or 30.0%. The trace is clean for policy purposes — 100% coverage, 207 fixes at a 10-second interval, no gaps, maximum gap 0 seconds — so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c) and the excess is established on the trace under POL-RD-01. It is below the 50% / 8.0 km materiality gate, so POL-RD-06 is not engaged and no driver-conduct referral arises.

Why no refund is due. The chat log (EV-CHAT-02811) contains the rider's own message at 06:33:18 — 'can we stop at Jurong Point first, need to grab something' — sent one minute after the meter started at 06:32:18, that is before the vehicle left the optimal corridor, followed by the driver's 'ok'. The waypoint_hint the platform resolved from that message (lat 1.305461, lng 103.90726) is corroborated by the trace: the nearest fix is 21.70 m away, well inside POL-RD-04's 200 m threshold. All three conditions of POL-RD-04(a) to (c) are therefore met — the instruction was the rider's, was timely, and named a specific place — and the excess between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor, which is the detour to and from Jurong Point, is excluded before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied. With that stretch removed no excess is left to found a deviation, the driver has discharged the burden POL-RD-08 shifts to him by pointing to the chat_log and POL-RD-04, and POL-RD-01 gives NO_ACTION.

The rider's objection that this was 'a tour' is not supported. The only waypoint the trace approaches is the one the rider herself named, and the 6.09 km is the distance to it and back. The driver's statement that the rider asked for the stop is confirmed by the chat and the trace, not merely asserted.

The arithmetic offered for the rider does not issue. Charged_total was 34.00, and a recomputation against the booked 20.3 km / 27.4 min optimal would give a recomputed_fare of 27.4970, a difference of 6.5030 and a rounded 6.55. POL-RD-02 runs only against the adjusted optimal, and here the adjustment removes the whole excess, so no distance-or-time refund arises for the rider and the 0.50 de minimis question never falls to be asked.

Other lines. The fare is METERED with zero ERP and toll lines, so POL-RD-09 adds nothing and there is no billing-integrity referral. The rider was billed 26.4 km against a 26.39 km trace, so there is no unbilled-distance shortfall and no DRIVER_COMPENSATION. Neither profile decides anything about this trip: deviation_flags_90d is 1 over 348 completed trips, below both POL-RD-06 tests, and deviation_claims_60d is 1, below the POL-RD-08 threshold; the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter was flagged as context-only and is not used.

Two claims about the missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-02811-01, weight 0.0) were discarded by the referee for not naming the MISSING_ARTIFACT issue code and are not reinstated; in any event no party asserts an external traffic cause here, so no advisory is needed and POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged.

Result. The present state stands: the 34.00 charge is not refunded and no compensation is paid. The monetary effect is 0, below the 8.00 execution threshold, so this provisional ruling executes on issue, and either party may appeal under POL-GEN-04. Confidence is 0.90, capped by the full-weight artifacts (EV-CHAT-02811, EV-GPS-02811) that carry the deciding fact.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this was a metered RYDE_X trip, TRP-02811, from Blk 55 Lengkok Bahru to Blk 610 Clementi West St 1. The fare stands unchanged and nothing is refunded.

The distance figures. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-02811) measures 26.39 km against the platform's optimal route of 20.3 km (EV-TRIP-02811), an excess of 6.09 km — 30.0%. The trace is clean for policy purposes: 207 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100.0% coverage, no gaps, maximum gap 0 seconds, so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)–(c) and the deviation is established on its face under POL-RD-01.

It does not survive POL-RD-04. The chat log (EV-CHAT-02811) shows the rider asked at 06:33:18, one minute after the meter started, 'can we stop at Jurong Point first, need to grab something', and the driver agreed. That instruction comes from the rider, was given before the vehicle left the optimal corridor, and names a specific place — POL-RD-04(a)–(c). The platform resolved the waypoint from the message (waypoint_hint lat 1.305461, lng 103.90726), and the vehicle passes within 21.70 m of it at fix index 104 (derived.waypoint_approach, EV-GPS-02811), far inside the 200 m corroboration threshold. The whole of the 6.09 km excess is the distance of that rider-requested stop between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor, and POL-RD-04 excludes it before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied. No deviation remains, so no refund arises.

On the rider's points. Your measurement — 26.39 km against 20.3 km — is accurate, but you asked for the stop, and POL-RD-04 is the answer to it. Your assertion that you 'only asked for a quick stop, not a tour' does not change the outcome: the place you named is what required the extra distance, and the trace shows the driver drove to it. The driver's statement that the stop was requested is borne out by the chat log, and I have not used the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter, which is context-only under POL-GEN-01.

On the arithmetic claims. Because POL-RD-04 fully excuses the excess, POL-RD-02 does not run — it applies only 'where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01 and no exculpatory clause fully excuses it'. The computed recomputed_fare of 27.4970 against a charged_total of 34.00, giving a refund of 6.5030 (6.55 payable) and 19.13% of the charge, is therefore not payable. The fare is METERED and not upfront-quoted, so POL-RD-11 is not the operative clause either; the point is simply that POL-RD-02 never engages. The claim that the record does not support the full 9.00 contested is correct, for the reason given.

Other checks. The fare carries zero ERP gantries and 0.00 in tolls, so there is no POL-RD-09 pass-through correction and no billing-integrity referral. The distance billed, 26.4 km, is not less than the 26.39 km trace, so there is no unbilled-distance shortfall and no POL-RD-04 driver compensation. The deviation is 30.0%, below the 50% / 8.0 km materiality gate, and the driver's deviation_flags_90d of 1 over 348 completed trips is below both POL-RD-06 pattern tests, so no repeat-pattern uplift and no driver-conduct referral. The traffic-advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-02811-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0, and no party relied on a traffic cause, so it carries nothing here.

No clause on these facts produces a referral, so the referrals list is empty. The monetary effect is nil, below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold. This ruling is provisional and may be appealed once under POL-GEN-04. Two claims in the brief that cited the missing advisory without disclosing its impairment were discarded and are recorded below.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties. The record decides this case, and it decides it against the claim.

The trip ran 26.39 km against a booked optimal of 20.3 km (EV-TRIP-02811; trace figure EV-GPS-02811). That is an excess of 6.09 km, or 30.0%, which clears both POL-RD-01 tests (over 20%, over 0.8 km) and would on its own be a deviation.

The rider's own in-app message defeats it. MSG-02811-001 (EV-CHAT-02811), sent by the rider at 06:33:18 — one minute after the meter started, before the vehicle left the optimal corridor — reads 'can we stop at Jurong Point first, need to grab something', and the driver answered 'ok'. The message names a specific place, and the platform's resolved waypoint (lat 1.305461, lng 103.90726) is carried on the message. The trace corroborates it: the nearest fix to that waypoint is 21.70 m, far inside the 200 m test in POL-RD-04. The clause is therefore available, and the excess attributable to the requested stop is excluded before the threshold is re-run. Nothing above the threshold remains, no deviation survives, and the fare stands.

The rider says she asked for 'a quick stop, not a tour'. That does not change the result. POL-RD-04 contains no test of how long a requested detour may be, and on this record the 6.09 km excess is the distance out to the waypoint she herself named and back — the trace shows no separate unexplained departure. The driver's counterparty statement ('the rider asked for the stop, it is in the chat') is borne out by the log.

For completeness, had a deviation survived, the POL-RD-02 arithmetic would run: recomputed fare 27.4970 against charged_total 34.00, a refund of 6.5030 rounded up to 6.55 — 19.13% of the charge, a partial refund and not a full one. It does not run, because the deviation is exonerated.

No referral arises. The deviation is 30.0%, below the 50% / 8.0 km materiality gate, and the driver's profile shows deviation_flags_90d of 1 against completed_trips_90d of 348, far below both POL-RD-06 pattern tests, so no driver-conduct review. The fare breakdown (EV-FARE-02811) carries no ERP, toll or surcharge line, so there is no billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09 and nothing to refer. No traffic advisory covers this trip (EV-ADVIS-02811-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0) and neither party relied on an external traffic cause, so POL-RD-03 plays no part and no escalation under POL-RD-10 follows from its absence.

The trace is clean for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 — 207 fixes, a 10 s interval, 100% coverage, no gaps — and the finding rests on artifacts at full weight (EV-CHAT-02811 and EV-GPS-02811, both 1.0), so confidence is not discounted. This provisional ruling moves no money; the charge is left as it stands. Each party may appeal once, within 30 days, through the help channel.

ruling.explanation:
Rider and driver: the charge for trip TRP-02811 stands. No refund is payable.

What the record shows. The trip runs from Blk 55 Lengkok Bahru, Bukit Merah to Blk 610 Clementi West St 1. The GPS trace EV-GPS-02811 (weight 1.0; 207 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100.0% coverage, no gaps, so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c)) records 26.39 km against the booked optimal of 20.3 km on EV-TRIP-02811 — an excess of 6.09 km, or 30.0% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests are met (over 20% and over 0.8 km), so a deviation is established on the trace.

Why it is exonerated. The chat log EV-CHAT-02811 carries the rider's own message MSG-02811-001, sent at 06:33:18 — 60 seconds after the meter started at 06:32:18, before the vehicle left the optimal corridor — reading 'can we stop at Jurong Point first, need to grab something'. The driver replied 'ok'. The message comes from the rider, is timely, and names a specific place carried by the platform as the resolved waypoint_hint (lat 1.305461, lng 103.90726). POL-RD-04 also requires the trace to corroborate the instruction, and it does: the nearest fix to that waypoint is 21.70 m away at 06:49:38, far inside the 200 m threshold. The rider asked for the stop, the driver made it, and the measured excess is the distance of that excursion out to Jurong Point and back to the booked route. POL-RD-04 excludes that excess before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied. Nothing above the POL-RD-01 thresholds remains, so no deviation survives and no refund is due. The rider's description of the trip as 'a tour' is not borne out: the only waypoint the trace approaches is the one she named, and the driver's statement that she asked for the stop is confirmed by the chat.

The money. The fare is METERED, so POL-RD-11 does not close the arithmetic route. For transparency: charged_total is 34.00, and on EV-FARE-02811 (weight 1.0) a POL-RD-02 recomputation against the booked optimal of 20.3 km / 27.4 min gives a recomputed fare of 27.4970 and an arithmetic refund of 6.5030, i.e. 6.55 payable — the figure the fare breakdown and the rider's own arithmetic claim put forward. That is not the computation that runs here, because POL-RD-04 requires it to be run against the adjusted optimal once the rider-requested excursion is excluded; on the adjusted optimal (26.39 km, duration scaled to 35.6 min) the recomputed fare is about 34.36, at or above the 34.00 charged, so the refund floors at zero. Neither the 6.55 figure nor the rider's contested 9.00 is payable, and the 90%-of-charged full-refund question therefore does not arise. The fare breakdown carries no ERP or toll lines (erp_lines.total 0.00), so POL-RD-09 pass-through corrections add nothing and no billing-integrity referral is produced.

The parties' other points. The rider bears and has discharged her initial burden under POL-RD-08: the trip identifier TRP-02811 matches across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, and the excess was shown; the driver in turn pointed to a specific artifact (the chat log) and a specific clause (POL-RD-04), which shifts and discharges the burden. No repeat-deviation pattern is established — driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 (below the 3-flag test) and 1 divided by 348 completed trips in 90 days is 0.0029 (below the 0.05 test) — so POL-RD-06 is not engaged, the 30.0% deviation is below the 50% / 8.0 km materiality gate, and no driver-conduct referral issues; the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is context only and has not been used. The rider_profile fields deviation_claims_60d (1) and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated (0) do not trigger the POL-RD-08 serial-claimant corroboration requirement, and no profile field is used to establish anything about this trip. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02811-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 and carries nothing; no live claim relies on it, so POL-RD-03 is not in play. No driver compensation is due: the rider was billed 26.4 km against a 26.39 km trace, so there is no unbilled shortfall above 1.0 km.

Confidence and effect. My confidence is 0.9. The fact this ruling turns on — that the excess is the rider-requested stop — is carried by two independent artifacts at full weight, the chat log EV-CHAT-02811 and the GPS trace EV-GPS-02811, so the cap is 1.0. The ruling is NO_ACTION: payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 are left as they are, and because the monetary effect is nil there is nothing to hold, well inside the SGD 8.00 execution threshold.
